diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any bounded function $v : [0,1] \times \mathbb{R}^{3d} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the time and spatial H\"older-Lipschitz condition: \[ \|v(t,x,y,z) - v(t',x',y',z')\| \leq C \left( |t - t'|^{1/2} + |x - x'| + |y - y'| + |z - z'| \right)

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma uh_regularity (ii) only gives |u_h(t,·)-u_h(s,·)| <= C_0(|t-s|^{1/2}+h^{1/2}), i.e. u_h is piecewise constant in t with jumps of size O(sqrt(h)); it does not satisfy the pure (1/2)-Holder hypothesis |v(t)-v(t')| <= C|t-t'|^{1/2} under which the mollifier estimate \|v-v^\varepsilon\|_\infty <= 2C\varepsilon of (v_varp_estimate) is proved. Consequently the claimed bound \|u_h-u_h^\varepsilon\|_\infty <= 2C_0\varepsilon is false as written; the correct estimate is <= 2C_0(\varepsilon+h^{1/2}). The derivative bounds in (uheps) already carry the (\varepsilon+h^{1/2}) prefactor, so only the sup-norm claim is affected.

failure_location.quote: \|u_h - u_h^{\varepsilon}\|_{\infty} \leq 2C_0 \varepsilon, \quad \|\partial_t^l D_x^k u_h^{\varepsilon}\|_{\infty} \leq 2C_0 K_{\zeta} (\varepsilon + h^{1/2}) \varepsilon^{-2l-k}, \quad \forall k,l \in \mathbb{N}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2C_0\varepsilon by 2C_0(\varepsilon+h^{1/2}) in (uheps) (and likewise in the initial-gap estimate at t=h); the extra O(\sqrt h) is dominated by the existing C_0 h^{1/2} terms and the conclusions of Theorems main theorem and main theorem CLT are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The \|u_h-u_h^\varepsilon\| and the comparison constants in the proof of the lower bound of Theorem main theorem are understated by an O(sqrt(h)) amount; the final lower bound acquires an extra O(C_0 h^{1/2}) term, which is absorbed by the already present h^{1/2}-terms, so the stated rates survive.
issues.title: Mollification estimates for u_h omit the O(sqrt(h)) grid-offset error
issues.why_classification: The defect is a local misapplication of a standard mollifier estimate; adding the h^{1/2} term preserves every claim and rate, so the repair is routine and lossless.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate splits |Δ_x ω|^{q_1} = |Δ_x ω|^{q_1-δ}|Δ_x ω|^δ with q_1 = 3/2 and bounds the first factor by (2‖D_xω‖_∞)^{q_1-δ}. This requires q_1 - δ >= 0, i.e. δ <= 3/2. Since p_1 = 3 is already maximal (Assumption assump2 (iv) only gives M_{X_1}^3 < ∞), q_1 = 3/2 is the smallest admissible conjugate, so the split is legitimate only for δ <= 3/2. Assumption assump2 (v) instead allows any δ ∈ ((3/4)α ∨ 1, α), and for α ∈ (3/2, 2) this range contains δ > 3/2, where the displayed interpolation has a negative exponent and is invalid (indeed false: for ω(x,y,z) = A sin x · sin(Nz)/N with fixed N, the true consistency error is O(h^{1/α - 1/2}) while the claimed δ-term decays like h^{(4δ-3α)/(6α)} with (4δ-3α)/(6α) > (2-α)/(2α) when δ > 3/2). Consequently Lemma consistency (and the E_1/E_2 bounds and rates derived from it) is not established for δ ∈ (3/2, α); in particular the claim sup_δ (4δ-3α)/(2α(2δ+3)) = 1/(4α+6) is overstated — with δ capped at 3/2 the best achievable exponent in that regime is (2-α)/(4α).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Assumption assump2 (v) to δ ∈ ((3/4)α ∨ 1, α ∧ 3/2) (i.e. split the increment with exponent ε* = min(δ, 3/2) ≤ q_1 = 3/2), and restate the rates Γ(α,δ,q_0) with δ so restricted; the architecture, proofs and rate structure survive unchanged, only the admissible δ-range (and hence the best rate for α ∈ (3/2,2), which becomes (2-α)/(4α) instead of 1/(4α+6)) narrows.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency estimate of Lemma consistency, the error bounds of Theorem main theorem (through E_1, E_2), the convergence-rate theorem for the universal robust limit theorem (main theorem CLT), and the example rates of Theorems main theorem ex1 and main theorem ex1 CLT (including the advertised sup_δ rate 1/(4α+6)) are unsupported for the permitted parameter regime δ ∈ (3/2, α), α ∈ (3/2,2); they remain valid only for δ ≤ 3/2.
issues.title: Hoelder interpolation in the consistency estimate is invalid for delta > 3/2, so the advertised rates are overstated
issues.why_classification: The defect is a contained invalid inference (a Hölder interpolation used with a negative exponent). The supported resolution — capping δ at the Hoelder-conjugate bound 3/2 and re-deriving the rate with δ* = min(δ, 3/2) — requires no new proof architecture and leaves a recognizably comparable convergence-rate theorem, only weakening the achievable exponent in the α ∈ (3/2, 2), δ > 3/2 sub-regime; hence moderate, not serious.
